name: Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City
description: Near Hangzhou on China's south-eastern coast, Liangzhu holds the remains of a walled city built some 5,000 years ago by a rice-farming Neolithic society. Its earthen city walls, palace and ceremonial areas, and graves ranked by status show a organised early state. Dams and channels form the earliest known water-control system in the world. Floods may have helped bring the city to an end.
